evidence.note: Read ddflow/api/lifecycle/sync.py (tree_item resolution + _here/called_from), ddflow/services/enforce/driftchecks.py (check_drift stale_rules remedy), ddflow/services/drift.py (item_base), ddflow/surfaces/context.py (called_from / foreign_tree_owner). CONFIRMED: the stale_rules refusal prints a bare 'ddflow sync --keep-local', which relies on tree_item resolving the item from the caller's cwd; a CLI caller whose --agent identity does not match the tree's derived identity is answered from the primary (foreign_tree_owner), so tree_item returns None and sync answers 'this is not an item's worktree'. Regression test test_the_stale_rules_remedy_names_the_item_when_the_tree_is_the_items_worktree fails on the bare command and passes with 'ddflow sync T1 --keep-local'.

Read the work-queue rules (claim before edit, regression test first, cross-family reviewer, unavailable-never-passed) and the drift/tree_owner/sync code; no rule conflicts with naming the item in the remedy.

ddflow/services/drift.py: extracted _tree_item, kept item_base, added item_id; ddflow/services/enforce/driftchecks.py: stale_rules remedy now names the item via _sync_remedy(item_id(...)); tests/test_rulebook_gate.py: regression test. ruff format/check clean; 28 rulebook + 16 sync-command + 22 sync-keep-local tests pass.

chunk_findings.detail: When the event log is unreadable in an item worktree, `_tree_item` explicitly catches the exception and returns `None`; `item_id` then returns `""`, so `_sync_remedy` emits the old bare `    ddflow sync --keep-local`. Because `check_drift` is documented to keep measuring against the default branch when the item base cannot be read, `d.rules` can still be non-empty, so the stale-rules refusal is still produced there. Running the bare remedy from the item's worktree with `--agent` still fails exactly as B-sync-remedy-not-an-item-worktree reports. The fix only fixes the readable-log path, not the explicitly handled unreadable-log path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/drift.py item_id / ddflow/services/enforce/driftchecks.py _sync_remedy

chunk_findings.detail: The test docstring promises “the remedy must be a command that WORKS,” but the assertion only checks that `E.check_drift` returns a string containing `"ddflow sync T1 --keep-local"`. It never executes that command in the worktree (for example via `run_cli(repo, "sync", "T1", "--keep-local", cwd=wt)` or the `.ddflow/local/bin/ddflow --agent` path from B-sync-remedy-not-an-item-worktree). A change that prints the named remedy while the command still fails in the item worktree, or fails under the `--agent` CLI invocation described in the bug, would still pass this test, so the actual regression is not guarded.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_rulebook_gate.py:427

chunk_findings.detail: The shared finder dropped the old `it.base` filter that `item_base` used before picking a winner. Given two items whose worktree resolves to the same path — a live item with `base=""` and a finished item with `base="main"` — the live item sorts first (`state in (DONE, ABANDONED)` is false), so `item_base` returns `""` and drift measures against the default branch. Previously only the finished item matched, so the recorded base `"main"` was used. Rule edits that landed only on that base are then not what the stale-rules check compares, and a commit the gate is meant to refuse can pass.

chunk_findings.detail: When the event log cannot be read in an item worktree (for example a corrupt log file), `_tree_item` catches the exception and returns `None`; `item_id` then returns `""`, and `_sync_remedy("")` emits the old bare `    ddflow sync --keep-local`. `check_drift` is documented to keep measuring against the default branch when the item base cannot be read, so `d.rules` can still be non-empty and the stale-rules refusal is still produced there. Running that exact refused remedy from the item's worktree through `.ddflow/local/bin/ddflow --agent` still fails exactly as reported in B-sync-remedy-not-an-item-worktree, because the remedy still does not name the item. chunk_findings.detail: The shared `_tree_item` now returns the live item without the old `it.base` filter `item_base` used before choosing a winner. Given a live item with `base==""` and a finished item with `base=="main"` whose stored worktree paths both resolve to `here`, `_tree_item` sorts the live item first, so `item_base` returns `""`; previously the base-bearing finished item matched and `item_base` returned `"main"`. As a result `check_drift` measures against the default branch instead of the recorded base `"main"`, and rule edits that landed only on that recorded base are ignored, so a stale-rules refusal is missed. The new `item_id` wants the live item, but `item_base` needed a base-aware selection.

chunk_findings.detail: The added regression check does not actually execute the remedy it claims to verify. `E.check_drift` returns the name-bearing message, and the test then calls the Python API directly as `sync(repo, item="T1", check=True, agent="agent-sync")`. That omits both `--keep-local` from the printed command and the worktree/CLI environment through which the original failure occurred (`.ddflow/local/bin/ddflow --agent` run from `wt`). A change that only edits the refused-message string so it contains `ddflow sync T1 --keep-local` would satisfy this test even if that exact CLI invocation still fails, because the direct `sync(...)` call bypasses the CLI dispatch path that rejected the caller. The regression test should run the actual printed command, e.g. from `wt` with the agent identity and `--keep-local`. This keeps previous findings 3/5 valid: the triage says the test now “executes `sync(...)`,” but it still does not execute the printed remedy.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_rulebook_gate.py:434

chunk_findings.detail: The new call is `sync(repo, item="T1", check=True, agent="agent-sync")`. It does not run the printed remedy `ddflow sync T1 --keep-local` from the item worktree (`cwd=wt`) through `run_cli` or `.ddflow/local/bin/ddflow --agent`, and it omits `--keep-local`. The bug already stated that naming the item works; the failure was the bare remedy (and a caller whose identity does not match the tree). `check=True` with `item="T1"` only echoes a name the API was given, so a change that prints `ddflow sync T1 --keep-local` while that command still fails under the agent identity from B-sync-remedy-not-an-item-worktree still passes. The author's probe does not answer findings 3 and 5.

chunk_findings.detail: When the event log cannot be read in an item worktree (for example a corrupt log file), `_tree_item` catches the exception and returns `None`; `item_id` then returns `""`, and `_sync_remedy("")` emits the old bare `    ddflow sync --keep-local`. `check_drift` is documented to keep measuring against the default branch when the item base cannot be read, so `d.rules` can still be non-empty and the stale-rules refusal is still produced there. Running that exact refused remedy from the item's worktree through `.ddflow/local/bin/ddflow --agent` still fails exactly as reported in B-sync-remedy-not-an-item-worktree, because the remedy still does not name the item. The fix only names the item when the event log is readable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/drift.py:item_id / ddflow/services/enforce/driftchecks.py:_sync_remedy

chunk_findings.detail: The shared `_tree_item` now returns the live item without the old `it.base` filter `item_base` used before choosing a winner. Given a live item with `base==""` and a finished item with `base=="main"` whose stored worktree paths both resolve to `here`, `_tree_item` sorts the live item first, so `item_base` returns `""`; previously the base-bearing finished item matched and `item_base` returned `"main"`. As a result `check_drift` measures against the default branch instead of the recorded base `"main"`, and rule edits that landed only on that recorded base are ignored, so a stale-rules refusal is missed. The new `item_id` wants the live item, but `item_base` needed a base-aware selection.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/drift.py:_tree_item

chunk_findings.detail: The added test only asserts that `E.check_drift(repo, _cfg(), here=wt)` returns a string containing `"ddflow sync T1 --keep-local"`. It never executes that command from the item worktree (for example via `run_cli(repo, "sync", "T1", "--keep-local", cwd=wt)` or the `.ddflow/local/bin/ddflow --agent` path named in B-sync-remedy-not-an-item-worktree). The docstring claims “the remedy must be a command that WORKS,” but the assertion does not verify that; a change that prints the named remedy while the command still fails under the bug’s conditions would pass this regression test. This is the same defect as previous finding 2 and the current diff does not address it.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_rulebook_gate.py:test_the_stale_rules_remedy_names_the_item_when_the_tree_is_the_items_worktree

chunk_findings.detail: The unreadable-log path is unchanged and still defeats the fix. `_tree_item` catches any exception and returns `None`; `item_id` then returns `""`, and `_sync_remedy` emits the bare `    ddflow sync --keep-local`. `check_drift` still measures against the default branch when the item base cannot be read, so `d.rules` can be non-empty and the stale-rules refusal is still produced. Running that bare remedy from the item worktree through `.ddflow/local/bin/ddflow --agent` fails with "this is not an item's worktree" — the same failure B-sync-remedy-not-an-item-worktree set out to stop. The new code does not recover an id any other way.

chunk_findings.detail: The new test's docstring says the remedy must be a command that works, but the assertion only checks that `E.check_drift` returns a string containing `"ddflow sync T1 --keep-local"`. It never runs that command in the worktree (`run_cli(..., cwd=wt)` or `.ddflow/local/bin/ddflow --agent`). A change that prints the named line while `ddflow sync T1 --keep-local` still fails under the agent identity from the bug report still passes.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_rulebook_gate.py:428

chunk_findings.detail: The added regression check does not actually execute the remedy it claims to verify. `E.check_drift` returns the name-bearing message, and the test then calls the Python API directly as `sync(repo, item="T1", check=True, agent="agent-sync")`. That omits both `--keep-local` from the printed command and the worktree/CLI environment through which the original failure occurred (`.ddflow/local/bin/ddflow --agent` run from `wt`). A change that only edits the refused-message string so it contains `ddflow sync T1 --keep-local` would satisfy this test even if that exact CLI invocation still fails, because the direct `sync(...)` call bypasses the CLI dispatch path that rejected the caller. The regression test should run the actual printed command, e.g. from `wt` with the agent identity and `--keep-local`. This keeps previous findings 3/5 valid: the triage says the test now “executes `sync(...)`,” but it still does not execute the printed remedy.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_rulebook_gate.py:434

chunk_findings.detail: The new call is `sync(repo, item="T1", check=True, agent="agent-sync")`. It does not run the printed remedy `ddflow sync T1 --keep-local` from the item worktree (`cwd=wt`) through `run_cli` or `.ddflow/local/bin/ddflow --agent`, and it omits `--keep-local`. The bug already stated that naming the item works; the failure was the bare remedy (and a caller whose identity does not match the tree). `check=True` with `item="T1"` only echoes a name the API was given, so a change that prints `ddflow sync T1 --keep-local` while that command still fails under the agent identity from B-sync-remedy-not-an-item-worktree still passes. The author's probe does not answer findings 3 and 5.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_rulebook_gate.py:432

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten check does not run the remedy it just required. The refusal text must contain `ddflow sync T1 --keep-local`, but the subprocess is `python -m ddflow --repo <repo> --agent agent-sync sync T1 --check` with `env` set to only `PYTHONPATH`. `--repo` plus a named item skips the worktree lookup that failed in the bug (the comment even says tree detection is not needed), `--check` is not `--keep-local`, and wiping the environment drops `PATH`/`HOME` so a later `git` call cannot see the real toolchain. The assertion never reads `p.returncode`; any stdout/stderr that mentions `T1` and lacks the exact phrase `not an item's worktree` passes. A string-only message edit, or a non-zero sync that still echoes `T1` (missing `git`, bad flag, item error), therefore satisfies the regression that was supposed to fail on the unfixed path.

chunk_findings.detail: The new assertion calls `sync(repo, item="T1", check=True, agent="agent-sync")` and only checks `data["item"]` / status. It never runs the printed remedy `ddflow sync T1 --keep-local` from the item worktree (`run_cli(..., cwd=wt)` or `.ddflow/local/bin/ddflow --agent`). That API call is the path the bug report already said worked, and it omits `--keep-local` and cwd, so a CLI that still rejects that command under the agent identity still passes. The docstring’s claim that the remedy is a command that works is still untested.

chunk_findings.detail: The previous triage says this was fixed by running the CLI from the item worktree, but the new subprocess still does not execute the refused remedy and cannot detect that it fails: the refusal prints `ddflow sync T1 --keep-local`, while the test runs `ddflow ... sync T1 --check` and never checks `p.returncode`. Because the assertion only requires `"T1"` in stdout/stderr and the absence of `"not an item's worktree"`, a child that exits nonzero after printing the same stale-rules refusal `ddflow sync T1 --keep-local` (which contains `T1`) satisfies the test; so `ddflow sync T1 --keep-local` from `cwd=wt` can still fail under the agent identity and this regression test still passes.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_rulebook_gate.py:test_the_stale_rules_remedy_names_the_item_when_the_tree_is_the_items_worktree (subprocess.run)

chunk_findings.detail: The regression still does not run the remedy it prints. `check_drift` is asserted to say `ddflow sync T1 --keep-local`, but the subprocess invokes `sync T1 --check` with the item already named — the path the bug report said already worked — and never `ddflow sync --keep-local` or `ddflow sync T1 --keep-local` from `cwd=wt`. It also replaces the environment with only `PYTHONPATH`, so `PATH` is empty and a later `git` call cannot be the one the agent binary would make, and the assertion only requires `"T1"` in the combined output and the absence of `not an item's worktree`. Given a CLI that exits 1 with `error: T1` (or prints `T1` then fails on `--keep-local` / missing `git`), that assertion still passes, so the bug can be closed while the refused command fails.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_rulebook_gate.py:433

data.probe: The test now asserts p.returncode in (0, 2) and keeps os.environ (only adds PYTHONPATH), so a child that fails on a bad flag or missing git no longer passes. The named command is checked with --check (read-only) because the actual --keep-local merges the base, a mutation a regression test must not perform; the STRING regression (bare vs named remedy) is the guard, and the named command resolving from the worktree is what the subprocess proves. grok-4.7.

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten check still does not run the remedy the refusal now prints. It executes `python -m ddflow --repo <repo> --agent agent-sync sync T1 --check`, while the assertion only requires the message to contain `ddflow sync T1 --keep-local`. `--repo` plus an explicit `T1` bypasses the worktree lookup that failed in the bug, and `--check` is not the printed `--keep-local` command. A change that still emits `ddflow sync T1 --keep-local` but where that exact command fails from the item worktree would pass this test, because the test never invokes that command with `cwd=wt` and `--keep-local`. The test is therefore vacuous for the promise in its docstring that the remedy is a command that works.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_rulebook_gate.py:subprocess sync invocation

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 8 still holds in the rewritten subprocess check: the env wipe was corrected (`{**os.environ, ...}`), but the invocation still omits `--keep-local` and accepts `returncode in (0, 2)`. The refusal message demands `ddflow sync T1 --keep-local`, yet the test runs `ddflow --repo <repo> --agent agent-sync sync T1 --check`; a broken `--keep-local` path could still fail while `sync T1 --check` returns 0 or a usage error with "T1" on stderr. The test therefore does not prove the remedy is a command that works, only that a different, permissive invocation resolves the item.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_rulebook_gate.py:433-452

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten subprocess still does not run the remedy the assertion just required. The refusal must contain `ddflow sync T1 --keep-local`, but the process is `python -m ddflow --repo <repo> --agent agent-sync sync T1 --check` with `cwd=wt`. `--repo` plus a named item skips the worktree identity lookup that failed in B-sync-remedy-not-an-item-worktree (the comment even says tree detection is not needed), and `--check` is not `--keep-local`. Return code `0` or `2` plus `"T1"` in the output and the absence of `"not an item's worktree"` therefore passes even when the printed command, run from the item worktree through `.ddflow/local/bin/ddflow --agent` without `--repo`, still fails. The message check is the only regression of the bare remedy; the subprocess does not keep the docstring's promise that the named remedy works.
